title: Version Control System — Git
description: Distributed version control; dominant in open source and industry.
body:
1. Tool identity. This record is the public-edition reference for Git, a version control system. Distributed version control; dominant in open source and industry. Category: Version Control and Collaboration.

2. Actual implementation. A working implementation ships inside this record as executable JavaScript (demo.program) and was executed in Node.js; the verified output is stored in demo.output. The demonstration exercises the tool's core behavior: [Git] log (2 commits): a1 init | b2 add parser || diff HEAD~1: +2 files changed, 28 insertions(+).

3. Inputs and outputs. This class of tool takes file changes and contributor actions and produces commit history, merge results, and issue states. The demonstration's input is a scenario selector (0-7); its output is the human-readable result line kept in demo.output.

4. Execution instructions. Requires Node.js 18 or later and nothing else. Save demo.program to a file, append a call such as console.log(demoMain(0, 'demo')), and run it with node. No dependencies are installed and no network is used.

5. Tests and examples. This record's demonstration scenario was executed in Node.js and its real output captured in demo.output. Re-running demoMain with the same scenario index reproduces it byte-for-byte.

6. Verification status. The record is marked tested: the shipped program was executed and its output verified. The reference facts about Git are public knowledge presented as reference.

7. Integration. Sibling records in this database document seven more version control system implementations. Compatible workflows: collaborate on code. The demo runs anywhere Node.js runs and composes with shell pipelines through stdout.

8. AI assistance. Troubleshooting: if the demo does not run, confirm Node.js 18+ is installed and the file was saved as UTF-8 without BOM. Documentation pointers: the reference tool's official project site and documentation. Improvement suggestions: extend the miniature with persistent state, richer scenarios, and error injection.
